title: BitMatrix::transpose 64x64 bit-block + AVX2
description:
Add a SIMD-accelerated $64 \times 64$ bit-block transpose kernel. The current implementation is naive $O(n^2)$ bit-by-bit and is a heavy hitter — many downstream operations transpose first.

## Background

`BitMatrix::transpose` at `crates/gf2-core/src/matrix.rs:858-870` is a naive double loop over individual bits. No SIMD, no register tiling.

The fix adds a new `transpose_fn` to the `LogicalFns` set (or a sibling `TransposeFns` registered via `simd::maybe_transpose()`):

- Scalar fallback: $64 \times 64$ bit-block transpose via Hacker's Delight ch. 7.3 (recursive bit-twiddle, $\sim 7$ stages of mask + shift + XOR).
- AVX2 SIMD: PSHUFB-based $8 \times 8$ byte tiles within YMM, then assemble $64 \times 64$ from 4 quadrants.
- Cache-layout outer loop: for $n > 8\text{K}$, drive a tiled outer loop that fits L1.

PPC walk: V0 baseline (add a new `transpose` bench targeting $n \in \{64, 256, 1024, 4096\}$ before any other edit) → V4 register tile + bit-twiddle → V3 SIMD via PSHUFB → V7 cache layout for large $n$. Target is $\geq 10\times$ on $n=4096$. If PSHUFB does not reach $10\times$, document why (cache-bound, bench too small) and either tune V7 layout or revert.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Proptest invariants hold: $\text{transpose}(\text{transpose}(M)) = M$, $M v$ matches $v^T M^T$ semantics.
- [hard] Word-boundary `#[test]`s pass at $n \in \{0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129\}$.
- [hard] No `unsafe` outside `gf2-kernels-simd`.
- [hard] New `transpose` bench committed and pinned to baseline `ppc-v0-2026-04-27`.
- [hard] Sibling `*.asm.txt` artefact for both bit-twiddle and PSHUFB paths committed.
- [hard] One commit per spiral step (V4 / V3 / V7).
- [aspirational] $\geq 10\times$ over baseline at $n=4096$.
